questions.question: What interface modality should the onboarding use: a CLI-based interactive wizard (like yeoman/create-react-app), a local web UI (like the swarm-manager console), or a TUI (terminal UI with rich widgets)?
questions.context: Vrooli currently has both CLI tools and web UIs (swarm-manager). The choice determines the tech stack, accessibility for non-technical users, and development effort. A web UI is friendlier but heavier; a CLI wizard is faster to build but less approachable.
options: CLI interactive wizard (fastest to build, consistent with existing tools)
Local web UI served by an onboarding API (most beginner-friendly)
TUI with rich widgets like bubbletea (good middle ground)
Hybrid: CLI for setup steps, then opens web UI for configuration

questions.question: What is the MVP scope for v1? Should it cover only initial first-run setup, or also serve as an ongoing configuration hub that users return to?
questions.context: The description mentions both first-time setup (resources, secrets) and ongoing configuration (autoheal settings, prompt-manager). These are different products — a setup wizard vs. a settings dashboard. Scoping this wrong means building twice.
options: First-run wizard only — guide through initial setup, then hand off to individual tools
Ongoing configuration hub — a central place users always come back to for all settings
First-run wizard for v1, with a roadmap to evolve into a configuration hub

questions.question: How non-technical is the target user? Are we designing for someone who has never used a terminal, or someone comfortable with CLI but unfamiliar with Vrooli specifically?
questions.context: Vrooli currently requires running shell scripts and managing config files. If the target is truly non-technical, the onboarding needs to abstract away the terminal entirely (web UI, point-and-click). If it is developers new to Vrooli, a guided CLI flow may suffice.
options: Non-technical: no terminal experience, needs full GUI
Semi-technical: comfortable with terminal basics, needs guidance on Vrooli concepts
Developer new to Vrooli: understands tools, just needs Vrooli-specific walkthrough

questions.question: Which resources and scenarios should the onboarding cover in v1? The system has 46+ resources — should it guide through all enabled ones, or focus on a curated starter set?
questions.context: Currently 46 resources are configured in service.json. Guiding through all of them would be overwhelming. A curated starter set (e.g. postgres, redis, ollama) would be more approachable for v1.
options: Curated starter set of essential resources only
All enabled resources with guided categorization
Let users pick from a checklist of available resources
